policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere רַגְלָי is 1cs (Ncfdc/Sp1cs), "my feet"; ketiv רגלו is 3ms (Ncfsc/Sp3ms), "his feet"; same lemma 7272. Solomon is quoting his own message about David, so the two readings put the enemies under different men's feet. The ASV reads "until Jehovah put them under the soles of his feet", continuing the third person of David my father ... his God, and no ASV note is mapped to the word. The possessor is visible in the English, so the ketiv is selected.
